source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Musculoskeletal strain, which more often follows exertion and lacks the typical pattern of an acute adnexal emergency.","B":"Primary dysmenorrhea, which usually follows a cyclic menstrual pattern rather than abrupt focal severe pain.","C":"Lower urinary infection, which more often causes urinary symptoms than abrupt, severe, one-sided pelvic pain.","D":"Ovarian torsion, which can cause sudden unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and needs urgent clinical evaluation."}}
source_row.rationale: Ovarian/adnexal torsion commonly presents with sudden abdominal or pelvic pain and nausea/vomiting and requires timely evaluation because torsion is a surgical diagnosis.
source_row.source_detail: Committee Opinion No. 783, Recommendations and Evaluation sections: sudden-onset intermittent abdominal pain with nausea/vomiting; timely diagnostic laparoscopy when torsion is suspected. ACOG Committee Opinion 783, August 2019; live ACOG clinical guidance rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client develops sudden severe unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting. Which condition requires urgent evaluation?
